Context: UA is purchasing Dedicated + Private control plane for production inference. Monthly committed capacity: 320k tokens/day, expected peak of ~600 qps during nightly indexing jobs. SLOs requested: 99.9% availability, 100ms p50 generation for 256-token sequences.

Immediate ask:
- Tessa: lead the kickoff and own the customer success program. Set cadence (kickoff + weekly 1:1s for 8 weeks).
- Ben: technical steward and primary for deployment work (VPC, canary config, model pinning).
- Marissa: onboarding materials and customer admin training; own success plan doc.

Risks we should track: billing alignment (contract shows usage-based overage terms), VPC peering timelines (might require 3rd party networking team), and model regression monitoring (they plan to test on live traffic).

Action items for this thread:
1) Propose 3 kickoff slots (next Tue/Wed/Thu morning PST) — Tessa to confirm availability.
2) Ben to draft a short technical plan and a canary checklist by EOD Friday.
3) Marissa to prepare a 30/60/90 success play and a short admin walkthrough deck.

Adding technical context and an initial checklist. High level notes:

- Network: UA will want VPC peering + private ENIs. Ops lead needs AWS account id for peering; estimate 3 business days once network ops is engaged.
- Capacity: committed baseline 320k tokens/day translates to ~120 concurrent sessions during peak. We'll map instance pools accordingly.
- Canary strategy: 2-week canary, start at 5% traffic -> 25% -> 50% -> 100% with metric gates at each step (error-rate, latency regressions, distributional drift on embeddings).
- Model variants: propose starting with rdl-7b-q4f and a 16-bit fallback for heavy queries. Need to confirm their prompt length distribution.

Draft owner matrix (short):
- CS Lead: Tessa Morgan — cadence, adoption metrics, success plan
- Tech Lead: Ben Carter — infra, deployment, canary execution
- Training/Admin: Marissa Cole — org admin, SSO setup, user training
- Executive sponsor: Karthik Iyer — escalation & commercial questions
Risks:
- If VPC peering delays >5 business days, we should stand up a temporary VPN tunnel to avoid slipping the start date.
- Budget risk if their usage spikes during indexing. Suggest alerting & daily cost reports in week 1.

I'll attach the draft deployment playbook and a short runbook template. Please review; I'll finalize for the kickoff.

Ben Carter
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference
